questions.question: Comprehension:निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें और दिए गए प्रश्न के उत्तर दें।गुजरात भारत के पश्चिमी तट पर स्थित है। गुजरात का इतिहास ईसवी पूर्व लगभग 2000 वर्ष पुराना है यह भी माना जाता है कि भगवान कृष्‍ण मथुरा छोड़कर सौराष्‍ट्र के पश्चिमी तट पर जा बसे, जो द्वारका यानी प्रवेशद्वार कहलाया। बाद के वर्षों में मौर्य, गुप्‍त, प्रतिहार तथा अन्‍य अनेक राजवंशों ने इस प्रदेश पर राज किया। चालुक्‍य (सोलंकी) राजाओं का शासनकाल गुजरात में प्रगति और समृद्धि का युग था। आजादी से पहले गुजरात का वर्तमान क्षेत्र मुख्‍य रूप से दो भागों में बंटा था- एक ब्रिटिश क्षेत्र और दूसरा देसी रियासतें। राज्‍यों के पुनर्गठन के कारण सौराष्‍ट्र के राज्‍यों और कच्‍छ के केंद्रशासित प्रदेश के साथ पूर्व ब्रिटिश गुजरात को मिलाकर द्विभाषी बंबई राज्‍य का गठन हुआ। पहली मई, 1960 को वर्तमान गुजरात राज्‍य अस्तित्‍व में आया। गुजरात का क्षेत्रफल लगभग 196,024 वर्ग किलोमीटर है। महात्मा गांधी और वल्लभभाई पटेल जैसे भारत के कई प्रसिद्ध व्यक्तियों की जन्मभूमि होने के कारण इस जगह की सांस्कृतिक और पारंपरिक विरासत बहुत समृद्ध है और ये राज्य का गौरव बढ़ाती है। गुजरात कपास, तंबाकू और मूंगफली का उत्‍पादन करने वाला देश का प्रमुख राज्‍य है । यहां की अन्‍य महत्‍वपूर्ण नकदी फसलें हैं- इसबगोल, धान, गेहूं और बाजरा। राज्‍य में भूतलीय जल तथा भूमिगत जल द्वारा कुल सिंचाई क्षमता 64.88 लाख हेक्‍टेयर आंकी गई है जिसमें सरदार सरोवर (नर्मदा) परियोजना की 17.92 लाख हेक्‍टेयर क्षमता है। राज्‍य में जून 2010 तक कुल सिंचाई क्षमता 31.65 लाख हेक्‍टेयर तक पहुंच गई थी। जून 2010 त‍क अधिकतम उपयोग क्षमता 23.79 लाख हेक्‍टेयर आंकी गई।गुजरात का इतिहास कितना पुराना है?

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. Waxing, a common method of hair removal, has been practised for centuries across different cultures and civilisations. While its basic purpose remains cosmetic, the motivations and perceptions surrounding waxing have evolved significantly. In ancient Egypt, hair removal was considered a symbol of cleanliness and beauty. Today, waxing is both a personal grooming choice and, at times, a reflection of societal norms and expectations. Modern waxing techniques range from traditional hot wax to newer options like sugar waxing and cold wax strips. These methods vary in effectiveness, pain levels, and cost, making accessibility and preference important factors in decision-making. Interestingly, the popularity of waxing has also prompted discussions about gender roles and body autonomy. Although once marketed predominantly to women, waxing has seen a rise in male clientele in recent years, reflecting a shift toward more inclusive beauty standards. Despite its widespread use, waxing is not without its criticisms. Dermatologists often warn against overuse, as it can irritate the skin, lead to ingrown hairs, and even cause long-term sensitivity. Moreover, some argue that the pressure to remove body hair is driven more by commercial beauty ideals than by individual preference. Waxing is more than a grooming habit; it reveals the complex interplay between personal choices, cultural influences, and evolving ideals of beauty.What does the passage suggest about the changing societal views toward waxing?
options: Waxing reflects broader changes in gender norms and self-expression.
Waxing has become less popular due to health concerns.
The motivations behind waxing are now solely aesthetic.
Ancient practices of waxing are no longer relevant today.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (Waxing reflects broader changes in gender norms and self-expression.) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.Public libraries have long been cornerstones of communities, offering a wealth of knowledge and resources for free. Beyond just books, libraries provide access to computers, Wi-Fi, meeting spaces, and a variety of programmes for all ages. This accessibility makes libraries crucial for individuals seeking to bridge the digital divide, gain new skills, or simply enjoy a quiet space to read or work.The rise of e-readers and online resources might seem like a threat to traditional libraries. However, libraries are adapting to the changing landscape. Many now offer digital collections of e-books and audiobooks, allowing patrons to access materials anytime, anywhere. Libraries also host workshops on digital literacy, helping individuals navigate the online world with confidence.Furthermore, libraries are increasingly becoming hubs for social interaction and community engagement. They host book clubs, author talks, and cultural events, fostering a sense of connection and belonging. Libraries also play a vital role in early childhood education, providing story times, educational resources, and a nurturing environment for young minds to explore and learn.In conclusion, libraries remain essential institutions in the 21st century. By offering a blend of traditional and modern resources, fostering social connections, and supporting education, libraries continue to empower individuals and communities to thrive.638Which of the following is a fact mentioned in the passage?
options: Libraries no longer provide a space for quiet reading.
Public libraries charge fees for access to Wi-Fi.

questions.explanation: M-ary QAM does not have constant energy per symbol. It also does not have constant distance between possible symbol states. It reasons that particular values of M-ary QAM signal will be detected with higher probability than others.

questions.question: Which decoding method involves the evaluation by means of Fano’s algorithm?
questions.explanation: Fano’s algorithm involves sequential decoding. It searches for the most probable path through the trellis by examining one path at a time.

questions.question: What must be used along with synchronous control inputs to trigger a change in the flip flop?
questions.explanation: A clock must be used along with synchronous control inputs to trigger a change in the flip flop. These flip – flops may be edge – triggered or level – triggered. A change should occur only when the clock changes from 0 to 1 or vice versa.

questions.question: [Test 7 - Q4] The Maria Montessori educational method is heavily characterized by:
options: Child-centered self-directed activity, hands-on learning, and collaborative play in prepared environments
Teacher-dominated lectures and strict penal punishments
Standardized paper-and-pencil exams conducted on a weekly basis
Pre-designed digital animations with no physical tactile materials
questions.explanation: Montessori classrooms feature prepared environments, multi-sensory materials, and self-directed learning tasks where teachers guide rather than lecture. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 7).

questions.question: [Test 65 - Q19] Which of the following is an example of an 'Intrinsic Motivation' factor in student learning?
options: Inherent curiosity and personal satisfaction derived from mastering a subject
Receiving cash prizes and gold medals from the school principal
Avoidance of parental disapproval or detention after school
Desire to secure first position in class merit list
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation arises from internal rewards—such as curiosity, interest, personal enjoyment, or autonomy—rather than external incentives or punishments. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 65).

questions.question: [Test 64 - Q16] Inclusive Education in Indian classrooms fundamentally implies:
options: Educating children with special needs alongside non-disabled children in regular classrooms with appropriate adaptations
Establishing separate special schools for children with disabilities
Admitting only high-achieving gifted students in mainstream schools
Providing home-based schooling for all children with mild learning difficulties
questions.explanation: Inclusive education ensures that all children, regardless of their physical, cognitive, social, or linguistic abilities, learn together in the same mainstream educational environment. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 64).

questions.question: [Test 60 - Q15] According to Robert Gagne's Conditions of Learning, how many hierarchical levels of learning are there, and what is the highest level?
questions.explanation: Gagne proposed 8 hierarchical levels of learning. The lowest is signal learning, and the highest, most complex level is problem-solving. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 60).

questions.question: [Test 61 - Q13] The 'Project Method' of teaching, which focuses on solving real-world, purposeful problems in a social environment, was developed by:
questions.explanation: Kilpatrick formulated the Project Method based on pragmatism and the educational philosophies of his mentor, John Dewey. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 61).

questions.question: [Test 37 - Q19] What is the primary objective of Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE)?
options: To evaluate all aspects of student development, including scholastic and co-scholastic domains continuously
To conduct quarterly written examinations to eliminate low performers
To substitute internal assessments with final external board examinations
To reduce teacher workload by automating grading systems
questions.explanation: CCE evaluates both scholastic (academic) and co-scholastic (life skills, attitudes, values) growth of a learner continuously throughout the academic cycle. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 37).

questions.question: [Test 24 - Q12] Under the Right to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009, what is the mandatory Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) prescribed for primary schools (Classes I to V)?
questions.explanation: As per the RTE Act 2009, the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for primary schools (Classes 1-5) is mandated at 30:1 for enrollment up to 200 students. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 24).

questions.question: [Test 50 - Q12] Which of the following principles best characterizes Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development regarding the process of Schema Adaptation?
questions.explanation: Piaget defined adaptation as the balance achieved through assimilation (incorporating new info into existing schemas) and accommodation (modifying existing schemas to fit new info). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 50).
